A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching proofs relocated between versions.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figure 2 report original trained-model accuracies on synthetic graph connectivity and iterated matrix multiplication tasks. Appendix G documents the experiments.

after.justification: Section 6 and Figure 2 retain the original synthetic-task experiments and model accuracies, with experimental details in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Definition 6 broadens the modeled PD transition class from permutation matrices to column-one-hot 0-1 matrices, permitting noninvertible transitions. This changes the admissible architecture class; the experimentally evaluated models remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate sorted deterministic graph connectivity and iterated 3 x 3 matrix multiplication over Z_m and Z. The represented data, task requirements, and length-extrapolation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Every Figure 2 comparison retains the same five models: nonlinear RNN, RWKV-7, DeltaNet, Mamba, and Transformer. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: The splits, length ranges, accuracy metric, model configurations, and training procedures are unchanged. Both versions retain the same discrepancy between Section 6's batch size 64 and learning rate 1e-4 and the appendix/Table 1's batch size 128 and learning rate 3e-4.

E4.justification: The same length-generalization analyses compare training-range performance with ranges [101, 200] and [201, 300]. Neither version adds distinct ablations, sensitivity analyses, error analyses, or case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run aggregation, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Their uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 2's plotted accuracies are identical, and Section 6 retains the same findings for all model-task combinations and length ranges. No empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: V3 substantially revises the PD analysis: Definition 6 permits noninvertible column-one-hot matrices, and Appendix C rederives their NC1 upper bound. Theorem 8 changes from PD–deterministic-WFA equivalence to one-way simulation of zero-threshold WFA languages, with Corollary 7 correspondingly qualified. Definition 2 adds max, and v1's Appendix H/Theorem 14 on input-dependent ReLU RNNs is removed.

C1.justification: The central nonlinear-versus-linear separation and complexity hierarchy remain. However, the PD classification now covers a broader transition class, while Section 5.2 narrows the claimed automata correspondence from exact equivalence to qualified one-way simulation.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly discusses parallelized nonlinear RNNs as components of hybrid models and explicitly leaves open whether their expressivity justifies the runtime overhead. Appendix D.1 adds that stacking LRNN layers may lose WFA representability while preserving the PNC1 bound.

D1.justification: The code-access link, benchmark generation and labeling instructions, model dimensions, and training hyperparameters are unchanged. V1 Appendix G becomes v3 Appendix F without substantive changes to experimental reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting circuit-complexity background, the PD proof, WFA stacking, and hybrid-model positioning, including Buss, Immerman and Landau, Mohri, and recent hybrid-model papers. Allender et al. (2017) disappears with Appendix H. Previously anonymous papers are identified without becoming new cited works.

P1.justification: Section 2.5 expands background explanations, and Section 4 incorporates the existing Theorem 3–4 proofs from v1 Appendix B. The PD discussion and conclusion receive localized rewrites, alongside terminology and publication-text edits; the overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 retain identical graphics, labels, and captions, and Table 1 retains its structure. Text reflow changes their surrounding placement, with Table 1 now occupying a separate final page; the publication footer also changes.

improvement.justification: V3 improves consistency between the PD definition and the deterministic-WFA construction, provides a matching generalized proof, and states the WFA theorem more carefully. Expanded background and moving core proofs into Section 4 improve accessibility. The separate input-dependent ReLU extension is lost, but the main MLP-based P-completeness result remains. Experimental evidence and reporting inconsistencies are unchanged, limiting the overall gain.
